title: (No AI) Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Suno v6 ai music model logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Suno_v6_Main.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Suno's new v6 [AI music model](https://suno.com/blog/introducing-v6) is its first made with support from the record industry. Suno's Jack Brody told _The Verge_ that v6 was "trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on." The data includes content licensed from partners [Warner Music Group](https://www.theverge.com/news/829189/warner-music-group-suno-ai-licensing-deal), [BMG](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/978232/suno-has-struck-a-global-alliance-with-the-music-company-bmg), and [Believe](https://suno.com/blog/believe-partnership), as well as "[user data](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/906896/sunos-copyright-ai-music-covers)." It's unclear whether that means v6 training data is completely free of [dubiously obtained content](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/966072/suno-ai-music-training-scraping-youtube-hack).

One of the big changes in v6 is that there are actually three different models: v6, v6-wild, and v6-mini. Mini is the model available for free to all. It's focused on fast, res …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/991977/suno-releases-its-first-ai-music-model-made-with-record-industry-help)

title: (No AI) OpenAI’s sly mathematical breakthrough sends a chill through academia
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/gettyimages-2292626872.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Open AI CEO Sam Altman speaks during the G20 Innovation Ministerial. | (Photo by Matt RAMEY / AFP via Getty Images)

OpenAI's announcement Tuesday that it has solved one of mathematics' legendary [Millennium Prize problems](https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/) should have been a moment of triumph. The result is both an undeniable achievement and a striking demonstration of just how [rapidly AI is transforming mathematics](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/977273/the-ai-takeover-of-mathematics-has-begun). But before it was even formally announced, the breakthrough had been complicated by the unusual circumstances that prompted OpenAI to pursue the problem: After hearing other researchers were making progress, it seems to have thrown its considerable resources into a last-minute effort to beat them to the punch. The ensuing controversy has surfaced allegations of scooping, spying …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/992953/openai-math-millennium-prize-navier-stokes)
